title: U.S. House · Colorado's 7th District
area: Parts of the western Denver metro area and foothills, including Arvada, Lakewood and Jefferson County.

context.text: Incumbent Brittany Pettersen (D) was unopposed in the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary. Timothy Bennett won the Republican primary over Amanda Capobianco.

summary.text: Brittany Pettersen is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Colorado's 7th District, first elected in 2022 as the first woman to represent the district. A Jefferson County native, she served a decade in the Colorado legislature before Congress and sits on the House Financial Services Committee. Her official biography says she is focused on mental health and substance use treatment, housing affordability, and consumer protection.

background.text: Born in Colorado and raised in Jefferson County. According to her campaign website, her father was a construction contractor and her mother a hairdresser, and her mother's addiction after being prescribed opioids shaped her interest in behavioral health policy.

Describes herself as the first in her family to graduate from both high school and college. Earned a B.A. in political science from Metropolitan State University of Denver, which her official biography says she paid for by waiting tables.
Before running for office, worked for New Era Colorado, a nonprofit that works to increase youth participation in politics.

Served in the Colorado House of Representatives (District 28) from 2013 to 2019. According to her campaign website, she chaired the House Education Committee and passed the Equal Pay for Equal Work Act, a red flag law, and the Secure Savings Act.

Served in the Colorado State Senate (District 22) from 2019 to 2023. Her official biography says her state legislative work included legislation on health care costs, the opioid epidemic, reproductive health care, and child care.

Won the open 7th District seat in 2022, defeating Republican Erik Aadland with about 56% of the vote, and was re-elected in 2024 over Republican Sergei Matveyuk with about 55%. She was unopposed in the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary.

Serves on the House Financial Services Committee, including the Subcommittee on Housing and Insurance and as Vice Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on National Security, Illicit Finance, and International Financial Institutions, according to her official biography.
According to her official biography, she lives in Lakewood with her husband, Ian, and their two sons.

record.text: Served on the House Committee on Financial Services (Housing and Insurance; National Security, Illicit Finance, and International Financial Institutions subcommittees) in the 118th Congress.
Introduced the Romance Scam Prevention Act, which passed both chambers of Congress; it would require dating platforms to notify users who interacted with an account removed for fraud.

Introduced the bipartisan Fentanyl Sanctions Reauthorization Act of 2026 with Rep. Roger Williams to extend sanctions authority against foreign fentanyl traffickers before it expires in December 2026.
Introduced the bipartisan Promoting Financial Literacy in Secondary Schools Act with Rep. David Valadao to give high schools access to financial literacy resources.

candidates.name: Timothy Bennett
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 30, 2026 Republican primary over Amanda Capobianco.

summary.text: Timothy Bennett is the Republican nominee for Colorado's 7th District, having advanced from the June 30, 2026 Republican primary as the only candidate on the ballot. A GoodParty.org profile lists him as a member of the Lewis-Palmer District 38 school board. Little additional biographical information from the candidate was found.

background.text: A GoodParty.org profile, built from public records and not claimed by the candidate, lists him as a Lewis-Palmer District 38 School Board member (District 1) with a term running 2026 to 2029.
Advanced from the June 30, 2026 Republican primary for the 7th District as the only candidate on the ballot, with 58,806 votes.

summary.text: Lawrence Clark is the American Constitution Party candidate for Colorado's 7th District. No biography, campaign website, or news profile was found.
Dan Sallis is the Libertarian Party candidate for Colorado's 7th District. No biography, campaign website, or news profile was found.

Joe Krzeczkowski is an unaffiliated candidate for Colorado's 7th District. He describes himself as a technology executive and software professional who has led global engineering teams. He says he is running to reform campaign finance, protect constitutional freedoms, and address housing, education, and infrastructure.

background.text: According to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, he was raised on a small family farm outside Ann Arbor, Michigan, and moved to Colorado in 2012.
Graduated from Saline High School and earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Michigan in 2011.
His career experience includes working as an engineer; he describes himself as a technology expert and software professional with experience leading global engineering teams.

summary.text: Susan Hall is the Unity Party candidate for Colorado's 7th District. She is a Denver native and teacher who describes herself as a third-generation Coloradan. Her 2024 Ballotpedia survey responses emphasize campaign finance reform and a ceasefire in Gaza.

background.text: Born in Denver, Colorado; graduated from Lincoln High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Metropolitan State University of Denver in 2003.
Her career experience includes working as a teacher. In a 2024 Ballotpedia survey response she described herself as a third-generation Coloradan, wife, mother, and teacher.

researchNotes: No Ballotpedia biography page was found for Republican nominee Timothy Bennett (page does not exist), or for minor-party/independent candidates Lawrence Clark, Dan Sallis, Joe Krzeczkowski, and Susan Hall; their entries are limited to their ballot listing from the Colorado 2026 House elections overview. No stated issue positions were found for Pettersen beyond her committee assignments for this basic-tier entry. Checked Pettersen's official issues pages (Congress, Economy, Education, Energy, Health, Veterans at pettersen.house.gov/issues), which contain no issue-specific text beyond category labels, and her recent press releases; none directly addressed a Position issue-key statement (bill topics found were fraud prevention, fentanyl sanctions, and financial literacy, added as record items instead). Biographies for Lawrence Clark and Dan Sallis could not be expanded because no biography, campaign site, or news profile was found; Timothy Bennett's rests on a single GoodParty.org public-records profile, and Joe Krzeczkowski's and Susan Hall's on their own Ballotpedia Candidate Connection responses (Hall's from 2024).
